title: COCA: Cost-Effective Collaborative Annotation System by Combining Experts and Amateurs
motivation: Expert annotation is expensive but necessary for precision; amateurs are cheap but cannot give precise labels for fine-grained tasks; existing methods need prior labeled data.
problem_framing: Formulate annotation as an optimization over cost ratio k between expert and amateur prices, minimizing total cost while achieving target precision.
key_insight: Experts only need to label 'pivot' samples (one per category) plus uncertain cases; amateurs do pairwise comparisons on ML-suggested similar pairs; ML model coordinates iteratively.
method_signature: Iterative three-agent system (expert/amateur/ML) with metric learning-guided annotation assignment and uncertainty-based sampling.
evaluation_criteria: Cost saving ratio vs k (price ratio) at same precision as SOTA automatic labeling models on fine-grained datasets.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: COCA requires k above threshold to outperform SOTA; real amateurs with mistakes need higher k thresholds than simulated amateurs.
evidence_for_taste: it would be inefficient to randomly pick data pairs
we don’t expect amateurs to do that
Amateurs don’t have to discover categories
metric learned on Stanford Dogs can better capture
thinking_moves: Exploit asymmetric costs between expert and amateur labor
Re-frame complex annotation as three-agent collaboration problem
Prove Lemma 1 to justify reference category selection theoretically
Iterate from zero prior knowledge by progressive label accumulation
Balance inter-category sample sizes and intra-category variance for ML training
